root_cause.text: nvme_dbbuf_set uses an off-by-one loop condition (`i <= dev->online_queues`) where `dev->online_queues` is a count of queues, so the valid index range is 0 to `dev->online_queues-1`, causing an out-of-bounds access when `i` equals `dev->online_queues`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the loop from `for (i = 1; i <= dev->online_queues; i++)` to `for (i = 1; i < dev->online_queues; i++)`. The commit description explicitly states: "dev->online_queues is a count incremented in nvme_init_queue. Thus, valid indices are 0 through dev->online_queues − 1." The KASAN report confirms a slab-out-of-bounds read in `nvme_dbbuf_set` during the loop iteration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in freeing DMA buffers for NVMe queues by adjusting loop condition.
intent_record.what: Changed loop bound from `i <= dev->online_queues` to `i < dev->online_queues` in the `nvme_dbbuf_set` function.
intent_record.how: The loop now iterates one fewer time, preventing access to the queue at index `dev->online_queues`, which is out of bounds if queues are indexed from 0 to `online_queues-1`.

grouping_result.intent: Fix off-by-one error in freeing DMA buffers for NVMe queues by adjusting loop condition.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the off-by-one loop condition error described in the vulnerability root cause by adjusting the loop condition to fix the out-of-bounds access.

candidates.rationale: The loop uses '<=' instead of '<', causing iteration up to index dev->online_queues when valid indices are only 0 to dev->online_queues-1. This leads to an out-of-bounds access when i equals dev->online_queues.

vuln_statements.explanation: The loop condition 'i <= dev->online_queues' causes an off-by-one error: dev->online_queues is a count of queues, so valid indices are 0 to dev->online_queues-1. When i equals dev->online_queues, an out-of-bounds access occurs, leading to a security vulnerability.
